thesis: This is an existing short, not a new idea, and the 2026-10-28 FOMC reinforced it: the Committee held at 3.75-4.00% on a 10-2 vote in which both dissenters wanted a HIKE, and the statement says inflation remains elevated. With the policy rate at 3.88% effective against a 4.99% 10-year and a 10y-2y curve of +38bp, the long end is repricing term premium and inflation persistence rather than following the funds rate, and a tightening-biased Fed removes the only bid that would reverse that.
key_risk: A hawkish hike into a slowing economy is exactly the setup that produces a violent long-end rally on growth fear, which would squeeze this short through 82 fast. Secondary: TLT has already fallen 7.8% from its 120-day high of 87.79, so the easy part of the move is behind it.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that shorting duration at a 4.99% 10-year is late — the yield has already repriced, and a December hike at 78c is consensus rather than insight. The answer is in what the long end actually did on the decision: TLT reversed from an intraday 81.76 to close 80.99, having rallied from 77.11 over the prior three weeks, and the curve steepened rather than inverted. A long end selling off on a hawkish hold while the curve steepens is pricing inflation and term premium, not recession — the recession case would show up as a flattening rally, and it did the opposite.

thesis: Gold is in a confirmed downtrend against a Fed that has stopped easing: price 373.51 sits below a stacked SMA20 (377.69), SMA50 (392.67) and SMA200 (413.56), and 26.7% below the 509.70 high. If the December hike lands into a slowdown and something in credit breaks, gold reprices up violently and a short is on the wrong side of the only asset that works in that scenario. Structural central-bank buying is also a bid that does not care about real rates, and it is the reason the 2026 drawdown has repeatedly found buyers.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that 26.7% off the high is where you cover a gold short, not open one: the position is only 2.8% above a 200-day low of 363.32, momentum shorts entered near support are how the frameworks own stop-distance rule gets violated, and gold already fell through the easing cycle, which means it is not actually trading on real rates the way the thesis claims. The entry answers it rather than arguing with it — the trade is only taken on a 376.50-381.50 retest, which is 1-2% ABOVE the market and into a level the tape has already rejected, so it fills on strength instead of selling the low. If gold instead breaks 363.32 directly, there is no trade.

catalyst.action: UPDATE to the long opened 2026-09-20 at 23.00 — hold, levels unchanged. The 23.00-24.10 zone is where the CEO himself bought; add there if it trades back, but not above 24.10.

thesis: An existing long, held, and the case has gotten sharper rather than staler. CEO Steve Cahillane joined in January 2026 to run the separation, paused it on 2026-02-11, redirected $700M into brand reinvestment instead — and then bought 213,106 shares of his own stock on the open market at $23.4616 on 2026-05-12, $5.0M of his own money committed after he owned the strategy rather than before. The stock is at 23.86 today, essentially his price. It trades at 9.9x trailing adjusted EPS of about $2.42 while beating consensus four quarters running, and the sell side is at a 3.7% bullish share with nine sell ratings, which is where the marginal seller has already sold.
key_risk: Packaged food is losing volume to private label and GLP-1-driven consumption change, and that is a structural headwind no amount of brand reinvestment reverses on a quarterly cadence — the $700M is a cost today against a benefit that may never show. The sell side being at 3.7% bullish is a contrarian setup only if the business stabilises; if it does not, 17 holds become 17 sells and the 9.9x becomes 8x. Specific near risk: the Oscar Mayer Deli Fresh packaging defect that drove most of the first-half share loss has to be behind them by this print.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that the CEO buy is six months stale and the stock has gone nowhere since — 23.46 in May against 23.86 now — so the market has had two quarters to agree with him and declined. Worse, a paused spin-off removes the one dated, mechanical catalyst that could have forced a re-rating, and what replaces it is a turnaround with no end date, which Cahillane said explicitly. The answer is only partial: the four consecutive beats (+4.8%, +14.2%, +8.6%, +4.4%) say the earnings base is not eroding while the multiple prices as though it is, and 9.9x with the stop below the 120-day low bounds what being wrong costs.

catalyst.action: WAIT for the print. Do not establish before 2026-11-02 after close — this company has missed consensus in three of its last four quarters and a pre-print entry is a coin flip on the one thing the thesis does not rest on. If guidance holds, enter in the 12.90-13.45 zone. If it gaps above 13.45, STAND ASIDE: the asymmetry here comes from buying near the floor seven insiders bought at, not from chasing a relief rally.

thesis: The reason Chemours trades at a reported 0.31x sales, 53.4% below its 200-day high, is PFAS liability — and in June 2026 that liability stopped being open-ended and became a number. The EPA settlement of 2026-06-24 is a $22.5M civil penalty in three annual installments plus $90M of mitigation over 15 years, and the North Carolina settlement is $455M over 15 years of which Chemours' share is roughly $180M on a net present value basis, stated as covered by existing accruals. Seven distinct insiders then bought stock on the open market in August, after the settlements and with no offsetting sales. The operating business behind that discount is not broken: TiO2 took a global price increase effective 2026-04-01 and Opteon refrigerants grew 37% year over year in the most recent quarter disclosed.
key_risk: Execution, not litigation, is what kills this: CC has missed consensus in three of its last four quarters (-2.7%, -29.1%, -23.4%, with the one beat off a near-zero base) and analyst revisions are deteriorating at -3.5pp. There is also a live securities class action in Delaware alleging misstatements about Opteon demand and 2026 guidance — the same Opteon line the bull case leans on. Liquidity and dilution: at $28.1M average daily dollar volume the name is tradeable but thin enough that an exit in a gap is costly, and a sub-$2.5B chemicals company carrying 15-year settlement obligations has an equity-raise path if TiO2 prices roll over. Sized at 2% for exactly that reason despite the conviction score.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that the insiders are already wrong: they bought at $14.95-15.62 in August and the stock made a NEW 200-day low of $12.49 on 2026-10-15, so the signal has been underwater for three months and the market has had a full quarter to agree with them. Partly answered by what the stock has done since that low — 12.62 to 13.36 over seven sessions, back above the SMA20 at 13.28 — but a 12% drawdown on a seven-buyer cluster is a real warning, and it is why the entry waits for the print rather than anticipating it.
